Why I'm a founder, not only a builder

I care about problems where technology, trust, and human outcomes overlap—especially in health and performance, where the cost of being wrong isn't a failed sprint, it's a broken promise to a person.

I founded and lead RoboTech Society at DePaul because communities are how you compound ambition: recruiting, teaching, and setting a quality bar that outlasts any single project.

I'm pursuing management education next because the founders I admire pair vision with capital discipline, org design, and narrative—and I'm building that stack on purpose.

Where I'm placing my next decade of bets

Continuous health, not dashboards

The opportunity isn't more data—it's trust, retention, and behavior change in preventive and wearable experiences people actually live with.

Intelligent machines in the real world

Robotics and human augmentation only win when teams respect safety, noise, and operations—not just demos. That's the bar I hold for anything I put my name on.

AI that earns a seat in the operating rhythm

Models matter when they change decisions: clearer feedback loops, accountable automation, and leadership that knows when to intervene.
